children: Scott Bessent has tried to impress upon investors that he has the power to move markets. Wednesday's bond market move shows a risk of that kind of talk-namely that the Treasury secretary might be raising expectations that could be difficult to meet.

Treasury yields, which rise when bond prices fall, climbed this morning after the Treasury Department said that it would buy up to $6 billion of 10-year to 20-year Treasurys at tomorrow's buyback operation. That is triple the number that the government has been buying in recent months but still disappointing to some investors who had been looking for something even larger.

Bessent had "set expectations really high" when he had emphasized last month that doubling the size of buybacks to $4 billion per operation was the minimum that he could do, said Leah Traub, a fixed-income portfolio manager at Lord Abbett.

The uptick in yields Wednesday reflects some disappointment Bessent didn't go bigger, Traub said. In addition, she said, the market had been somewhat paralyzed heading into the 11 a.m. ET announcement and was also responding to other developments like the rise in oil prices.
